title: Skill Hub Portable Test Case
description:
One `test-cases/<slug>/case.json` inside a Download Artifact (PACK-005, packaging-design.md §5). Sample files sit beside it under `test-cases/<slug>/data/`.

This schema is read in BOTH directions on purpose (04 丙-12): the packager exports Test Cases into it, and the curation seeding script under tools/content/ imports the same shape into a fresh deployment's catalogue workspace. Two schemas would become two formats, and the seeding path is exactly the one that does not exist yet.

ONLY CURATED CONTENT IS PORTABLE. A user's uploaded Dataset bytes are never packaged and no opt-in checkbox is offered: a checkbox looks like respecting the user's choice but actually hands a licensing judgement to the person least equipped to make it, about files that may belong to their employer (packaging-design.md §5.1). Run results, evaluations, traces, evidence excerpts and improvement-suggestion prose are Run data, not Skill content, and have no field here (iron rule 11, packaging-design.md §4.3).
$comment: sensitivity: no_secrets - curated content only; see the description.

schema_version.description: Portable Test Case contract version, MAJOR.MINOR. Same evolution rule as the other packaging contracts: minor bumps are additive, a breaking change bumps the major and gets a new $id.

slug.description: The directory name under `test-cases/`. Platform-generated and stable: the same Test Case packaged twice gets the same slug, which is what lets `manifest_hash` stay equal across two builds of unchanged content.

origin.description: How this Test Case came to be. The enum has exactly one value, and that is the point: the only content that may travel inside a package is platform-curated material with no user-uploaded bytes (CONTENT-007's synthetic, secret-free, PII-free criterion). Widening this is a product decision that must change the contract, not a flag an exporter can flip.

user_prompt.description: The task text a user would send (`test_cases.user_prompt`, TEST-001). Curated text.

criteria.description: Acceptance conditions (TEST-003). Only `id` and `text` travel: `source` and `confirmed_at` describe who proposed a condition and when a particular user agreed to its wording, which are facts about one workspace and do not survive the trip. On import they are re-established for the importing workspace.

id.description: Unique within this Test Case and stable across edits. Rubric items reference these ids.

rubric.description: The optional strengthening of the acceptance criteria (CONTENT-007 clause 3), same shape as `test_cases.rubric` (0026) plus the version string. Absent and empty are different statements: absent means this Test Case has no rubric, which is true of all 45 baseline test cases. A rubric is not a second mechanism - its items map onto the same criterion results.

items.description: The three fields the 0026 CHECK constraint requires on every stored rubric item, in their portable form. `id` must name a criterion of this same Test Case - a cross-reference JSON Schema cannot express, so the importer checks it, exactly as Go does for the stored form.

evidence_required.description: Whether the judgement on this item must quote evidence.

datasets.description: Sample files shipped under `test-cases/<slug>/data/`. Curated synthetic data only - a user's uploaded Dataset is excluded by `origin`, and its Test Case is reported in the manifest's `excluded_test_cases` with reason `user_uploaded_dataset` rather than silently dropped.

file.description: Path relative to this case.json, always a direct child of `data/`. Constrained rather than free-form because the user unpacks this to their own disk: the platform never unpacks to disk, so the import side has no zip-slip check, and the export side is where that check first becomes necessary (packaging-design.md §2.1, §4.4). No `..`, no absolute path, no backslash, no nesting.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's bytes, so the importer can verify what it got and the same value feeds `manifest_hash`.

examples.name: Monthly report from the sample ledger
examples.user_prompt: Read data/ledger-2026-06.csv and write a one-page summary of the month: total spend, the three largest line items, and anything that looks like a duplicate charge.

criteria.text: The total spend figure matches the sum of the CSV rows.
The three largest line items are named with their amounts.
Suspected duplicate charges are listed, or their absence is stated.

items.text: The total must be quoted as a number and be arithmetically correct.
A claim that there are no duplicates must name what was compared.

examples.name: Behaviour on an empty input
examples.user_prompt: Summarise the attached notes. There are none - say so rather than inventing content.

criteria.text: The reply states that no input was provided.
